terrainOutwardNormal.detail: The authoritative terrain mesh is drawn by its BACK faces (set the material to FrontSide and the ground vanishes, leaving only the world-box side walls). three's DOUBLE_SIDED therefore flips the authored upward vertex normal and lights the ground through a downward one, which inverts every slope-dependent term. Ordinary ground hides it, because its relief comes from the baked terrainShade computed from the TRUE normal and the direct lights are a small share of an environment-dominated scene. Metal ore does not hide it: its metalness/roughness reflection is lit entirely through the normal, so a north-facing ore slope reflected and shaded as if it faced the southern sun. 'ore' restores the authored outward normal only where the ore region covers, fixing that and leaving every other pixel byte-identical. 'terrain' applies it to the whole surface - more physically correct, and a large change: the ground starts taking sky irradiance instead of floor irradiance and brightens substantially, so the biome palette and RenderLighting3D scales would want retuning. 'off' keeps the historical flipped normal for bisecting.

worldBox.detail: Water extends this far beyond every terrain edge AND this far below the world-box floor. The world-box walls descend by depthAverageAxisFraction × ((map width + map length) / 2), and both the land slab and the liquid are capped at their floor, so each is a closed solid.

presetBackdrop.detail: Four map-centered panorama shells, ordered near to terminal. Effective distance is max(minimumDistanceWorldUnits, distanceMapFactor times the larger map axis). The first three generated UASTC KTX2 textures are transparent RGBA scenery/cloud layers; terminal is the fully opaque sky and is the only layer allowed to contain stars. verticalOffsetDegrees applies to all four: 0 is authored placement, negative lowers, positive raises. Generator blur must increase with distance.

mapPresetLabel.detail: Map caption standing on its own slab of terrain just outside the map's (0,0) corner — the near-left corner at the default camera yaw. Exact stock settings show the preset name; changed settings show CUSTOM while retaining current map details. Font sizes are canvas pixels and set the block's internal proportions; blockHeightMapFraction scales the whole block against the larger map axis, so the caption keeps the same on-screen size at whole-map zoom on every map. cornerMarginMapFraction is how far off the map edge the block stands, also in map-axis units. groundLift is world units above the water surface, and puts the plinth's grassy TOP face there. plinthPadBlockFraction is the terrain border around the caption and plinthThicknessBlockFraction the slab's depth, both in caption-block heights. The letters are extruded out of the painted glyph mask: letterDepthTitleFraction is their height as a fraction of the title font, letterMaskSupersample how much finer than the painted caption the traced mask is, and letterMaskSimplifyPx the outline simplification tolerance in mask pixels (larger = fewer triangles, blockier glyphs).

vegetationWeathering.detail: Weathering for everything that grows - world-unit bark/foliage/grass projection, soil at the base of each plant, dry patches dissolved through the live colour, and dust on upward-facing surfaces. false restores uv-space texture repeats and flat foliage; keep it as a bisect and as the lever if the extra fragment work ever matters, since vegetation is the most numerous thing in the world. Tuning lives in colorsConfig.environment.vegetationWeathering.

terrainWallWear.detail: The worn top and bottom rims of a D-PLATEAU wall. false draws the fold the mesh describes, which is the clean terrace edge this treatment replaces - keep it as a bisect. Tuning lives in colorsConfig.world.terrain.wallWear. Intensity is driven by the dihedral angle measured at each rim, so a wall flattened flush into the terrain wears nothing: the treatment must never draw a step the map author deliberately erased.

terrainOreEdge.detail: The weathered ore-to-ground transition (warped contour, granular dissolve, dirt band). false draws the region field's own contour straight, which is the clean stencilled edge this treatment replaces - keep it as a bisect. Tuning lives in colorsConfig.environment.metalDeposit.edge. A SURFACE = METAL world switches it off on its own: the whole map is ore there, so every deposit boundary is interior and a dirt band around one would be drawing a seam that does not exist.

tree.detail: textureRepeat is gone on purpose: the bark and leaf tiles are projected from world position at an authored WORLD size (colorsConfig.environment.vegetationWeathering) rather than sampled through the models' uvs. Through uvs at a fixed repeat, a big tree and a small tree wore bark at different physical sizes.

entityShadow.detail: darknessPercent is the contact shadow's OWN strength. It used to borrow fogConfig radarDarknessPercent, so changing how dark radar contacts look also changed how dark unit shadows were. 35 is that value, so the look is unchanged and the coupling is gone.
